newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. blasts court order on welfare benefits.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. blasts court order on welfare benefits.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson sharply criticized a court order temporarily blocking a state law that would reduce welfare benefits to certain families.

"Narrow special interests are attempting to require the state to spend more of the people's money than their duly elected legislative representatives have determined," Wilson, a Republican, said in a statement.

Attorneys for the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) sued the state to block the law, alleging that reductions in so-called "Temporary Assistance to Needy Families" benefits would violate the U.S. Constitution.
The law would reduce benefits to recipients who have not lived in California for 12 consecutive months to the levels they received in the states they had left.
At a hearing in Sacramento, Judge Lawrence Karlton issued a temporary restraining order, blocking California from enacting the state law and its welfare reductions.

The restraining order will remain in effect until May 16 when a hearing on a preliminary injunction will be held, the ACLU said. Wilson said he was confident the courts would allow the law to take effect.
